name: ICCRN Myofascial PT
question: Does targeted pelvic floor myofascial physical therapy improve symptoms more than global therapeutic massage in women with IC/BPS and pelvic floor tenderness?

design.blinding: single-blind; participants and outcome assessors masked
design.population: Women with IC/BPS for 3 months to 3 years, bladder pain, urgency and frequency ratings of at least 3/10, and pelvic floor tenderness confirmed by a study physical therapist.

verdictNote: Global response improved; individual symptom scales showed no significant between-group difference.
takeaway: Targeted myofascial physical therapy produced more moderate or marked global improvement than global therapeutic massage at 12 weeks in women with IC/BPS and pelvic floor tenderness (23/39 [59.0%] versus 11/42 [26.2%]; P = 0.0012).

reports.label: 12-week randomized comparison
reports.citation: FitzGerald MP, Payne CK, Lukacz ES, et al. "Randomized Multicenter Clinical Trial of Myofascial Physical Therapy in Women With Interstitial Cystitis/Painful Bladder Syndrome and Pelvic Floor Tenderness." *J Urol.* 2012;187(6):2113-2118. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2012.01.123
reports.followUp: Primary assessment at 12 weeks; 3-month post-treatment follow-up was incomplete.

results.measure: Moderately or markedly improved at 12 weeks; risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Seven-category assessment. Difference calculated from reported rounded arm rates; center-adjusted exact conditional Mantel-Haenszel P value. Missing primary outcomes counted as nonresponse.

results.note: Difference in mean changes calculated from table values; complete follow-up data only.

harms.label: At least one adverse event
harms.note: P = 0.73. Overall, 12/81 (14.8%) had a severe adverse event; pain was reported by 14% of participants. No serious adverse events were reported.

delivery.label: Sites
delivery.locator: PMC3351550 PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods

delivery.label: Treatment protocol
delivery.value: Up to ten 60-minute sessions over 12 weeks; targeted internal and external manipulation of pelvic floor, hip girdle and abdominal muscle and connective tissue versus full-body Western massage.

delivery.label: Therapist preparation
delivery.value: Site physical therapists were centrally trained and certified in both interventions.

delivery.label: Treatment and study completion

values.exp: 38/39 completed 12 weeks; 21/38 completers received all ten sessions
values.ctl: 40/42 completed 12 weeks; 15/40 completers received all ten sessions

delivery.note: Enrollment closed at 81 versus a planned 88 owing to slow accrual and limited funding.

delivery.label: Post-treatment follow-up

values.exp: 30/39 had partial data; 23/39 completed final GRA
values.ctl: 28/42 had partial data; 11/42 completed final GRA

delivery.note: During the 3 months after treatment, 4/30 MPT and 8/28 massage patients with partial data received additional MPT.
